stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 4(3x − 2) + 5x + 6?
A. 17x − 2
B. 17x + 14
C. 12x − 2
D. 7x − 2

distractor_rationales.B: Distributed as 4(3x + 2) = 12x + 8 instead of 12x − 8, giving 12x + 8 + 5x + 6 = 17x + 14
distractor_rationales.C: Omitted the 5x term; computed only 12x − 8 + 6 = 12x − 2
distractor_rationales.D: Subtracted the 5x term instead of adding: 12x − 8 − 5x + 6 = 7x − 2

why_this_difficulty: Easy: single distribution then collect; all integer coefficients.

A. 5x − 10
B. 5x − 14
C. x − 10
D. 5x + 14

distractor_rationales.C: Subtracted the 2x term instead of adding: 3x − 12 − 2x + 2 = x − 10

why_this_difficulty: Easy: two distributions, integer results; common errors are sign flips in one factor.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 9x² + 3x − 4x² + 7x − 5?
A. 5x² + 10x − 5
B. 5x² − 4x − 5
C. 13x² + 10x − 5
D. 5x² + 10x + 5

distractor_rationales.B: Treated +7x as −7x when collecting: 3x − 7x = −4x
distractor_rationales.C: Added x² coefficients instead of subtracting: 9 + 4 = 13 instead of 9 − 4 = 5
distractor_rationales.D: Changed sign of constant: −5 → +5

why_this_difficulty: Easy: three groups of like terms; no distribution required.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 6a³ + 2a − 3a³ + 5a?
A. 3a³ + 7a
B. 3a³ − 3a
C. 9a³ + 7a
D. 3a⁴ + 7a

distractor_rationales.B: Subtracted a terms instead of adding: 2a − 5a = −3a
distractor_rationales.C: Added a³ terms instead of subtracting: 6 + 3 = 9
distractor_rationales.D: Multiplied the a³ and a terms as if combining exponents: wrote a⁴

why_this_difficulty: Easy: pure collection across two variable types; no distribution.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 12x³ + 8x²?
A. 4x²(3x + 2)
B. 2x²(6x + 4)
C. 4(3x³ + 2x²)
D. 4x(3x² + 2x)

distractor_rationales.B: Used GCF coefficient 2 instead of 4; the remaining terms 6x and 4 still share a common factor
distractor_rationales.C: Factored out only the numerical GCF 4, not the variable part x²
distractor_rationales.D: Factored out 4x instead of 4x²; one power of x remains un-factored

why_this_difficulty: Easy: monomial GCF with two terms; students must extract both the numerical factor and the variable factor.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 5x(x − 3) + 2(x − 3)?
A. (5x + 2)(x − 3)
B. (5x − 2)(x − 3)
C. (5x + 2)(x + 3)
D. 5x(x − 3) + 2

distractor_rationales.B: Changed the sign of the 2: used −2 instead of +2 in the linear factor
distractor_rationales.C: Changed the sign of the common binomial factor: (x + 3) instead of (x − 3)
distractor_rationales.D: Factored out (x − 3) from only the first term; did not complete the factoring

why_this_difficulty: Easy: the common binomial factor is explicit; students just read off the remaining linear factor.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ∛(x^5)?
A. x^(5/3)
B. x^(3/5)
C. 5x^(1/3)
D. x^15

distractor_rationales.B: Flipped the numerator and denominator: wrote 3/5 instead of 5/3
distractor_rationales.C: Moved the inner exponent 5 outside the radical as a coefficient instead of keeping it in the exponent
distractor_rationales.D: Multiplied the indices 5 × 3 = 15 instead of writing 5 as the numerator over 3

solution_steps: Recall: the nth root of x^m equals x^(m/n)
why_this_difficulty: Easy: direct application of radical-to-rational-exponent conversion rule.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x^(2/3)?
A. ∛(x²)
B. √(x³)
C. ∛(x³)
D. x²/3

distractor_rationales.B: Flipped the exponent: x^(3/2) = √(x³), not x^(2/3)
distractor_rationales.C: Used the same root index 3 but dropped the numerator 2: ∛(x³) = x, not x^(2/3)
distractor_rationales.D: Misread the rational exponent as an algebraic fraction: interpreted x^(2/3) as (x²)/3

solution_steps: Recall: x^(m/n) = nth root of x^m
why_this_difficulty: Easy: reverse conversion from rational exponent to radical form.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x² + 7x + 12?
A. (x + 3)(x + 4)
B. (x + 2)(x + 6)
C. (x + 1)(x + 12)
D. (x − 3)(x − 4)

distractor_rationales.B: Chose factor pair {2, 6} with correct product 12 but wrong sum: 2 + 6 = 8 ≠ 7
distractor_rationales.C: Chose factor pair {1, 12} with correct product 12 but wrong sum: 1 + 12 = 13 ≠ 7
distractor_rationales.D: Used negative factors; (x − 3)(x − 4) = x² − 7x + 12, not x² + 7x + 12

solution_steps: Find two integers with product 12 and sum 7: 3 × 4 = 12 and 3 + 4 = 7
why_this_difficulty: Easy: monic trinomial with positive coefficients; distractors test other factor pairs.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x² − x − 6?
A. (x − 3)(x + 2)
B. (x + 3)(x − 2)
C. (x − 3)(x − 2)
D. (x + 3)(x + 2)

distractor_rationales.B: Reversed the signs: (x + 3)(x − 2) = x² + x − 6, giving the wrong sign on the middle term
distractor_rationales.C: Used both negative: (x − 3)(x − 2) = x² − 5x + 6, both middle term and constant are wrong
distractor_rationales.D: Used both positive: (x + 3)(x + 2) = x² + 5x + 6, all terms positive

solution_steps: Need two integers with product −6 and sum −1
why_this_difficulty: Easy: monic trinomial with mixed signs; sign tracking is the key skill.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 2x² + 5x − 3?
A. (2x − 1)(x + 3)
B. (2x + 1)(x − 3)
C. (2x + 3)(x − 1)
D. (x + 3)(x − 1)

distractor_rationales.B: (2x + 1)(x − 3) = 2x² − 6x + x − 3 = 2x² − 5x − 3; middle term has wrong sign
distractor_rationales.C: (2x + 3)(x − 1) = 2x² − 2x + 3x − 3 = 2x² + x − 3; middle term is wrong
distractor_rationales.D: Dropped the leading coefficient 2; (x + 3)(x − 1) = x² + 2x − 3, not a degree-2 match

solution_steps: Find factors of 2x² and −3 that combine to give +5x
why_this_difficulty: Easy: non-monic trinomial; must find factors of both leading coefficient and constant.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to (2x + 3)(x − 5)?
A. 2x² − 7x − 15
B. 2x² + 7x − 15
C. 2x² − 7x + 15
D. 2x² − 15

distractor_rationales.B: Sign error: computed +10x − 3x = +7x instead of −10x + 3x = −7x
distractor_rationales.C: Sign error on constant: used 3 × 5 = +15 instead of 3 × (−5) = −15
distractor_rationales.D: Computed only the first and last products; omitted the middle cross terms entirely

why_this_difficulty: Medium: FOIL with mixed signs; middle-term sign errors are the primary trap.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to (3x − 1)(3x + 1)?
A. 9x² − 1
B. 9x² + 1
C. 9x² − 6x − 1
D. 6x − 2

distractor_rationales.B: Added the constant instead of subtracting: did not recognize the difference-of-squares pattern
distractor_rationales.C: Treated as (3x − 1)² instead: (3x − 1)² = 9x² − 6x + 1, then also got the sign wrong
distractor_rationales.D: Added the two binomials instead of multiplying: (3x − 1) + (3x + 1) = 6x − 2

solution_steps: Recognize difference of squares: (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²
why_this_difficulty: Medium: difference-of-squares pattern; students who FOIL mechanically may still get the right answer, but pattern recognition is the intended skill.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to (x + 2)(x² − 3x + 4)?
A. x³ − x² − 2x + 8
B. x³ − x² + 10x + 8
C. x³ + x² − 2x + 8
D. x³ − x² − 2x − 8

distractor_rationales.B: Sign error: computed 2·(−3x) as +6x instead of −6x, giving −3x² + 2x² + 4x + 6x + 8 = −x² + 10x + 8
distractor_rationales.C: Sign error on x² term: computed −3x² + 2x² = +x² instead of −x²
distractor_rationales.D: Sign error on constant: computed 2·4 as −8 instead of +8

solution_steps: Distribute x: x·x² − x·3x + x·4 = x³ − 3x² + 4x
why_this_difficulty: Medium: linear × quadratic multiplication; tracking three groups of partial products raises error risk.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to (4x² + 3x − 7) + (2x² − 5x + 1)?
A. 6x² − 2x − 6
B. 6x² + 8x − 6
C. 2x² − 2x − 6
D. 6x² − 2x − 8

distractor_rationales.B: Ignored the sign of −5x; added magnitudes: 3 + 5 = 8 instead of 3 + (−5) = −2
distractor_rationales.C: Subtracted x² terms instead of adding: 4 − 2 = 2 instead of 4 + 2 = 6
distractor_rationales.D: Constant error: computed −7 + 1 = −8 by treating it as −7 − 1

why_this_difficulty: Medium: polynomial addition with a negative coefficient; sign tracking on the x term is the main challenge.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to (5x² − 3x + 8) − (2x² + x − 4)?
A. 3x² − 4x + 12
B. 3x² − 4x + 4
C. 3x² − 2x + 12
D. 7x² − 4x + 4

distractor_rationales.B: Distributed the minus sign to x term but not to the constant −4; computed 8 − 4 = 4 instead of 8 − (−4) = 12
distractor_rationales.C: Distributed minus to the constant but not the x term; computed −3x − x as −3x + x = −2x instead of −4x
distractor_rationales.D: Added x² terms instead of subtracting: 5 + 2 = 7

solution_steps: Distribute the minus sign to all terms of the second polynomial: −(2x² + x − 4) = −2x² − x + 4
why_this_difficulty: Medium: polynomial subtraction; distributing the minus sign to every term — especially to a negative constant — is the critical step.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x⁵ · x³?
A. x⁸
B. x¹⁵
C. 2x⁸
D. x²

distractor_rationales.B: Multiplied exponents instead of adding: 5 × 3 = 15
distractor_rationales.C: Added a coefficient of 2; there is no basis for doubling the coefficient here
distractor_rationales.D: Subtracted exponents instead of adding: 5 − 3 = 2

why_this_difficulty: Medium: product rule applied directly; the main traps are multiplying or subtracting exponents.

Which of the following is equivalent to (x⁴)³?
A. x¹²
B. x⁷
C. x⁶⁴
D. 3x⁴

distractor_rationales.B: Added exponents instead of multiplying: 4 + 3 = 7
distractor_rationales.C: Computed 4³ = 64 as the new exponent instead of 4 × 3 = 12
distractor_rationales.D: Moved the outer exponent to become a coefficient: wrote 3x⁴

why_this_difficulty: Medium: power-of-a-power rule; students often confuse multiply vs. add, or treat the outer exponent as a coefficient.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 4x⁻²?
A. 4/x²
B. −4x²
C. 4x²
D. −4/x²

distractor_rationales.B: Interpreted the negative exponent as a sign change on x: wrote −4x² instead of moving x² to the denominator
distractor_rationales.C: Dropped the negative exponent: 4x² ignores the reciprocal
distractor_rationales.D: Both moved x² to the denominator AND negated the coefficient: applied the negative twice

why_this_difficulty: Medium: negative exponent rule; students commonly confuse x^(−n) with −x^n.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x³ + 3x² − 4x − 12?
A. (x² − 4)(x + 3)
B. (x² + 4)(x + 3)
C. (x² − 4)(x − 3)
D. (x + 3)(x + 4)

distractor_rationales.B: Sign error when factoring −4(x + 3): treated as +4(x + 3), giving x² + 4 instead of x² − 4
distractor_rationales.C: Sign error in the common binomial factor: used (x − 3) instead of (x + 3)
distractor_rationales.D: Incorrect expansion: (x + 3)(x + 4) = x² + 7x + 12, which does not match the original cubic

why_this_difficulty: Medium: factor by grouping on a cubic; recognizing the common binomial is the key insight.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 4x²y + 8xy²?
A. 4xy(x + 2y)
B. 2xy(2x + 4y)
C. 4x(xy + 2y²)
D. 4xy(x + 2)

distractor_rationales.B: Used GCF of 2xy instead of 4xy; the resulting terms 2x and 4y still share a common factor 2
distractor_rationales.C: Factored out only x from the GCF, missing the y; GCF is 4xy not 4x
distractor_rationales.D: Dropped the y in the second factor term: 4xy · 2 = 8xy, not 8xy²

why_this_difficulty: Medium: multi-variable GCF; students must extract both variable parts of the GCF correctly.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x² + 6x + 5?
A. (x + 3)² − 4
B. (x + 3)² + 5
C. (x + 6)² − 31
D. (x + 3)² − 9

distractor_rationales.B: Wrote (x + 3)² and then appended the original constant +5, without subtracting the 9 that completing the square added
distractor_rationales.C: Tried (x + 6)², but (x + 6)² = x² + 12x + 36 has the wrong coefficient for x; the half-coefficient is 3, not 6
distractor_rationales.D: Completed the square correctly to (x + 3)², then subtracted only 9 without adding back the original constant 5; net adjustment should be −9 + 5 = −4

solution_steps: Take half the x-coefficient: 6/2 = 3; square it: 3² = 9
why_this_difficulty: Hard: completing the square to reveal vertex form; the two-step constant adjustment (−9 + original c) trips up most students.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to x² − 8x + 7?
A. (x − 4)² − 9
B. (x − 4)² + 7
C. (x − 4)² − 16
D. (x − 8)² − 57

distractor_rationales.B: Wrote (x − 4)² and appended the original +7 without adjusting; did not subtract 16 to compensate for the square
distractor_rationales.C: Subtracted 16 (the square completion value) as the net constant, ignoring the original +7; should be −16 + 7 = −9
distractor_rationales.D: Used (x − 8)² instead of (x − 4)²; (x − 8)² = x² − 16x + 64 has the wrong x-coefficient

why_this_difficulty: Hard: completing the square with a negative x-coefficient; sign errors inside the square and in the net constant are both traps.

stem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 1/(x + 2) + 3/(x − 1)?
A. (4x + 5)/[(x + 2)(x − 1)]
B. 4/[(x + 2)(x − 1)]
C. (4x + 5)/(2x + 1)
D. (4x + 7)/[(x + 2)(x − 1)]

distractor_rationales.B: Added numerators directly without adjusting for the LCD: 1 + 3 = 4
distractor_rationales.C: Added denominators instead of multiplying to find the LCD: (x + 2) + (x − 1) = 2x + 1
distractor_rationales.D: Arithmetic error when expanding 3(x + 2): computed 3x + 8 instead of 3x + 6, giving (x − 1) + (3x + 8) = 4x + 7

why_this_difficulty: Hard: adding rational expressions with linear denominators; students must expand and combine the adjusted numerators correctly.
sat_key_phrases: Which of the following is equivalent to

distractor_rationales.B: Added numerators without adjusting for LCD: 3 + 2 = 5
distractor_rationales.C: Added the denominators instead of multiplying: (x + 4) + (x − 2) = 2x + 2
distractor_rationales.D: Sign error: used 2(x − 4) = 2x − 8 instead of 2(x + 4) = 2x + 8 when cross-multiplying the second term, giving 3x − 6 + 2x − 8 = 5x − 14

why_this_difficulty: Hard: adding rational expressions; expanding each numerator using the other denominator is the key multi-step process.

stem:
If (x − 2) is a factor of x² + kx − 10, which of the following is the value of k?
A. 3
B. −3
C. 5
D. −5

distractor_rationales.B: Found the factor pairing (x + 2)(x − 5) instead: k = 2 + (−5) = −3, which gives x² − 3x − 10, not the original
distractor_rationales.C: Read off the other root value (+5) directly instead of computing k = sum of roots: gave 5 instead of 5 − 2 = 3
distractor_rationales.D: Used the other root with a sign error: −5 instead of +5 as the second root, then k = 2 + (−7)...

solution_steps: Since (x − 2) is a factor, x = 2 is a root: substitute 4 + 2k − 10 = 0
why_this_difficulty: Hard: working backwards from a known factor to find an unknown coefficient; requires substituting the root and solving.

stem:
Which of the following is a factor of x² − 2x − 15?
A. x + 3
B. x − 3
C. x + 5
D. x − 15

distractor_rationales.B: (x − 3)(x + 5) = x² + 2x − 15; correct constant but wrong sign on the middle term
distractor_rationales.C: (x + 5) would require a root at x = −5; checking: (−5)² − 2(−5) − 15 = 25 + 10 − 15 = 20 ≠ 0
distractor_rationales.D: The constant −15 is not a factor in the polynomial-factor sense; a factor has the form (x − r)

solution_steps: Factor: find two integers with product −15 and sum −2
The factor (x + 3) appears in the choices
why_this_difficulty: Hard: recognizing factors from sign patterns; distractors use the same numbers with wrong signs.

stem:
The expression (2x + 1)(x² − 3x + 4) is expanded and written in standard form. What is the coefficient of x²?
A. −5
B. −6
C. 1
D. 5

distractor_rationales.B: Computed only the product 2x · (−3x) = −6x² and omitted 1 · x² = x²; missing the second x² contribution
distractor_rationales.C: Computed only 1 · x² = x² and omitted 2x · (−3x) = −6x²; missing the first x² contribution
distractor_rationales.D: Found the magnitude 5 but dropped the negative sign

why_this_difficulty: Hard: finding a specific coefficient without fully expanding; requires tracking all partial products that produce x².

stem: The expression (x + p)(x + q) is equivalent to x² + 11x + c, where p and q are positive integers and p − q = 3. What is c?
solution_steps: Since (x + p)(x + q) = x² + (p + q)x + pq, we have p + q = 11 and c = pq
Add the two equations: 2p = 14, so p = 7; then q = 11 − 7 = 4
why_this_difficulty: Hard: two constraints on p and q must both be used; a common error is ignoring the p − q = 3 condition and guessing any pair that sums to 11.

stem:
Which value of x satisfies x^(2/3) = 9?
A. 27
B. 6
C. 3
D. 729

distractor_rationales.B: Multiplied instead of applying the reciprocal power: 9 × (2/3) = 6
distractor_rationales.C: Took only the square root of 9: √9 = 3, without cubing the result
distractor_rationales.D: Raised 9 to the power 3 instead of 3/2: 9³ = 729

solution_steps: Raise both sides to the reciprocal power 3/2: (x^(2/3))^(3/2) = 9^(3/2)
why_this_difficulty: Hard: solving an equation with a rational exponent by applying the reciprocal power; two-step process (square root then cube) is error-prone.

stem:
If 3^(2x) = 81, what is the value of x?
A. 2
B. 4
C. 8
D. 1/2

distractor_rationales.B: Found that 3⁴ = 81 and set x = 4, forgetting to divide by the coefficient 2 in the exponent 2x
distractor_rationales.C: Multiplied 4 × 2 = 8 instead of dividing: 4 ÷ 2 = 2
distractor_rationales.D: Inverted the coefficient: set x = 1/2 by treating '2x = 4' as 'x = 1/2' via some reciprocal error

why_this_difficulty: Hard: solving exponential equation by matching bases; students who find the correct base exponent often forget to divide by the coefficient of x.
